significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a sparse set of heads writes a causal "reconsider" signal and that dampening it produces a difficulty-dependent dissociation—"shortens easy-problem traces without accuracy loss but harms hard problems"—which is a form-(iii) conditional relation layered on a form-(ii) circuit claim. This would establish both a phenomenon, adaptive versus maladaptive verification under intervention, and a mechanism, namely that "the same circuit serves both" and is modulated by an upstream difficulty feature; it therefore predicts intervention effects outside the particular trigger tokens used to identify the circuit. A verified-false result would clearly rule out the sparse shared-gate and simple miscalibration account, although it would not distinguish distributed verification mechanisms from alternative triggers; thus the branches are determinate but asymmetrically informative. The topic-substitution check lowers no score: generic efficient-reasoning research would not itself imply this specific easy/hard reversal, which is more constraining than the blunt compute-allocation premise underlying methods such as Muennighoff et al.'s 2025 "s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling."

reach.justification: The named handle is the "targeted, interpretable knob" implemented through "graded head interventions—scaling attention output"; it is ex ante or online because it can suppress a verification loop before the redundant continuation and associated token cost occur, rather than merely explaining a completed trace. After recalibration on another model, the particular heads would need rediscovery, but the claimed easy-versus-hard intervention relation predicts what should recur—efficiency gains on easy cases and accuracy damage on hard ones—rather than supplying only an unconstrained search procedure. The asserted scope covers easy and hard reasoning problems but is qualified by possible sensitivity to "different RL recipes"; downstream users could include inference and deployment engineers controlling latency and cost, not only circuit researchers. The topic-substitution check passes because efficient reasoning alone supplies neither this difficulty-conditioned control rule nor the specific head-output knob, although the limited cross-architecture commitment prevents broader reach.
